description: This Wikipedia article is a crowd-sourced list of collapses of radio and television masts and towers around the world, from the early twentieth century to the present. Each entry gives the date, the structure and its location, its height and type (guyed mast or self-supporting tower) and the cause, such as storms, ice, fire, aircraft or helicopter strikes, engineering defects, accidents during maintenance, sabotage and war, with references to news and technical sources. Well-known examples include the collapse of the Emley Moor mast in England in March 1969 under wind and ice loading, and the many towers brought down by the ice storm in northern Michigan in March 2025. Because it spans many countries and decades, it is one of the few places where broadcast tower failures are gathered together, and it is widely copied by other sites. Coverage: worldwide, about 1900s to present. Format and access: wiki tables, free under CC BY-SA 4.0, downloadable through Wikipedia's export tools. Caveats: open editing; coverage favours English-language news and tall structures, and causes are as reported. Simulation uses: an event catalogue for estimating failure rates and causes of transmitter structures, choosing historical scenarios for broadcast outage studies and cross-checking hazard fragility assumptions. Related records: the CRREL icing failure data are a systematic US subset, and the Bilsdale transmitter fire case documents one event in depth.
